title: Annotatio VI §.II open: Posterior Class authors — Brenz, Andreae, Hunnius; Flacius mode; Formula of Concord swearers
pass_a_gloss: §. II. The Posterior Class of Controversies has as Authors and disputators, as to the matters most contested, the chief and most famous Doctors John Brenz (of the ubiquity or omnipresence of Christ’s Body), Jacob Andreae (of the oral manducation of this Body superadded), and Aegidius Hunnius (of Predestination from foreseen Faith); but as to the more acerbic mode of controverting, the Disciples of Flacius Illyricus, a man of most restless Ingenuity: in a word, those who — if not all, certainly the great majority — lead themselves to swear by the words of the Formula of Concord, even the damnatory ones, no less, in the very matter, than by the words of Holy Scripture itself.
pass_b_english: §. II. The posterior class has, for the hottest points, Brenz on the ubiquity or omnipresence of Christ’s body, Andreae on oral manducation of that body added on top, and Hunnius on predestination from foreseen faith.
For the harsher style of fight it has Flacius Illyricus’s disciples — a most restless ingenuity.
In a word: those who (if not all, then most) bind themselves to the Formula of Concord’s words — even the damnatory ones — as tightly as to Holy Scripture itself.
source_text:
§. II.
Posterior Controversiarum Classis Autores ac disputatores habet, quà res maximè controversas, Joh. Brentii, ubiquitatis seu omnipraesentiae Corporis Christi; Jac. Andreae, oralis hujus Corporis manducationis superadditae, & Aegidii Hunnii, Praedestinationis ex praevisa Fide, praecipuorum ac famosissimorum Doctorum; quà modum autem controvertendi acerbiorem, Flacii Illyrici, inquietissimi hominis Ingenii, Discipulos: Verbô unô, eos, qui si non omnes, certè quàm plurimi, in verba Formulae Concordiae, etiam damnatoria, non minus, re ipsâ, quàm in verba ipsius Scripturae S. sibi jurandum ducunt.
